catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction based on file symbols and project structure, not full source inspection. Focus on structural, domain, and data-flow patterns, excluding agentic patterns.
analysis_limits: Only file paths and symbols available; no full source code inspected.
Inference based on naming conventions and module structure.
Some patterns may be partially observed or speculative.

system_map.overview: The system is a CLI-based Continuous Architecture System (CAS) runner that orchestrates governance actions, manages knowledge artifacts, and evaluates skill compliance. It follows a layered architecture: user-facing CLI -> application services -> domain models and governance engines -> infrastructure (LLM clients, file IO). Pydantic models serve as the domain backbone, and a mix of service objects and registries provide structure and extensibility.

layers.name: Presentations/CLI
layers.purpose: Entry points for user interaction and command routing.

layers.name: Application
layers.purpose: Orchestrates workflows, runner logic, and service facades.

layers.name: Domain
layers.purpose: Defines domain entities, value objects, and state models using Pydantic.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.purpose: Handles external integrations (LLM clients), bootstrap setup, and low-level IO.

dependencies: LLM clients abstracted behind a common interface

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: All domain entities (skills, governance, health) are defined as Pydantic models, providing validation, serialization, and a consistent schema across layers.
patterns.intent: Centralize domain data structures and leverage Pydantic's validation and type safety for consistent input-output contracts.
patterns.context: The system deals with structured data like skill evaluations, governance inventories, and health metrics that must be validated and passed between services.
forces: Need for data validation across boundaries
Serialization to/from JSON for persistence and API interactions
Maintainability and clarity of domain entities
patterns.solution: Define all domain entities as Pydantic BaseModel subclasses, using field types, validators, and default values to enforce invariants. Models are reused across layers, ensuring type safety and reducing conversion errors.
implementation_signals: Used in service arguments and returns

evidence.note: Pydantic models for skill evaluation entities.
Models for governance and compliance data.
Health status model with calculation logic.

patterns.name: Service Layer Facade
patterns.summary: A service layer (e.g., GovernanceActionService) exposes high-level operations that encapsulate complex workflows, hiding underlying engines and repositories.
patterns.intent: Provide a simplified interface for clients and isolate business logic from infrastructure concerns.
patterns.context: The governance action workflow involves multiple engines (action engine, compliance engine) and data manipulation. Directly exposing these would create tight coupling.
patterns.solution: Introduce service classes that act as facades over domain engines. They orchestrate calls, handle transactions, and translate responses, while the CLI or Runner depends only on the service interface.
implementation_signals: Methods that delegate to underlying engines

evidence.note: Runner uses services to execute flows.

failure_modes: God service class accumulating too many responsibilities

patterns.name: LLM Client Adapter/Strategy
patterns.summary: Multiple LLM clients (LiteLLM, Mock) implement a common interface, allowing the system to switch providers or use mocks without altering dependent code.
patterns.intent: Decouple LLM invocation from specific provider implementations and enable easy testing and provider replacement.
patterns.context: The system needs to call LLM services (via Litellm) and also support a mock client for development and validation without external calls.
forces: Need to support multiple LLM providers
patterns.solution: Define a protocol/interface for LLM clients, implemented by LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient. Depend on the interface (e.g., dependency injection) so callers are agnostic to concrete implementation.
implementation_signals: Two or more classes with similar methods
Classes inheriting from a common base/protocol
Factory or DI to choose implementation

failure_modes: Mock not faithfully replicating real behavior

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: Governance states and allowed transitions are managed in a TransitionRegistry, which drives the GovernanceActionEngine as a state machine.
patterns.intent: Control state transitions in a structured, declarative way, preventing invalid state changes and enabling auditability.
patterns.context: Governance actions involve moving between states (e.g., draft, in-review, approved). The engine must enforce transition rules.
forces: Need for explicit rules on state changes
patterns.solution: Create a registry of allowed transitions (from-state, to-state, maybe conditions). The engine consults this registry to validate and execute transitions, centralizing rule logic.

evidence.note: Registry and engine for handling transitions.

failure_modes: Registry becoming out of sync with actual flow

patterns.name: Bootstrap Initialization Script
patterns.summary: A dedicated bootstrap module initializes the workspace, merges configuration blocks (e.g., CLAUDE settings), and sets up symlinks or copies.
patterns.intent: Centralize setup tasks to ensure a consistent project environment and configuration across teams.
patterns.context: The tool needs to be bootstrapped in CI or local environments, requiring merging of governance blocks from various files and creating symlinks.
patterns.solution: Provide a bootstrap function that orchestrates all initialization steps: check prerequisites, create dirs, merge config files, symlink/copy resources, and render onboarding checklist.

costs: May need regular updates as structure evolves
failure_modes: Merge logic incorrectly overwriting user settings

patterns.name: Health Metric Value Object
patterns.summary: Health status is modeled as a value object with computing functions (calculate_health) and reason generation, centralizing health logic.
patterns.intent: Encapsulate health computation and representation to provide consistent metric outputs.
patterns.context: The dashboard needs to compute system health based on various inputs and present reasons for the status.
patterns.solution: Define a HealthStatus model (value object) and pure functions that take inputs and return status and reasons. Keep logic separate from output rendering.

costs: May be overkill for simple metrics
Immutable value objects may not fit all needs
failure_modes: Mixing business logic into value object

patterns.name: Compliance Engine Validation
patterns.summary: A dedicated ComplianceEngine encapsulates validation rules and findings generation, enforcing governance compliance.
patterns.intent: Separate compliance checks from other business logic and create a reusable validation service.
patterns.context: The system must validate governance artifacts against rules and produce findings (warnings, errors).
patterns.solution: Implement ComplianceEngine that takes models/configurations, runs a set of checks, and returns list of ComplianceFinding objects. Engine can be extended with new check methods.

costs: May become complex with many rules
failure_modes: Checks tightly coupled to specific models

patterns.name: Agentic Config Merger
patterns.summary: AgenticMerger merges governance blocks from multiple config files (e.g., AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) using a systematic merging algorithm.
patterns.intent: Combine conflicting configuration sections without manual intervention, ensuring consistency.
patterns.context: The system needs to merge configuration blocks from various agent specification files that may overlap.
patterns.solution: Implement a merger class with methods to merge specific governance block types, using rules to combine content while preserving uniqueness.

costs: Potential data loss if not comprehensive

anti_patterns.name: God Class Risk in Governance Service
symptoms: GovernanceActionService may accumulate many responsibilities if not kept focused.
Multiple engines and models handled in a single service.
suggested_remediation: Split service into smaller focused services

anti_patterns.name: Excessive Bootstrap Complexity
symptoms: bootstrap script handles merging, symlinking, checklist rendering in one place.
suggested_remediation: Break down into smaller steps with clear error handling

cross_cutting_concerns.description: Merging and management of configuration files across multiple agent systems (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, etc.).
Consistent validation of knowledge artifacts and governance actions.

open_questions.question: Are there other infrastructure abstractions for file IO or process execution beyond bootstrap?
open_questions.assumption: Currently only bootstrap handles file ops.

open_questions.question: How are state transitions persisted and audited?
